title: Commit split fallback for overlapping reserved capacity transfers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's reserved capacity transfer flow (used for tenant pool rebalances, org consolidations, and customer-initiated capacity moves) can produce transient double-counting or temporary negative available balances when transfers overlap calendar/epoch boundaries across regions. Existing purely eventual reconciliation produces billing blips and customer support tickets for high-throughput tenants.

Problem statement:
When two transfers touch the same quota ledger slice within a short window (e.g., transfer A moves 5,000 token-units from Pool X -> Y while transfer B concurrently moves a subset back or to another pool), we can see either: (a) an ephemeral double-commit where both transfers are applied before consistent re-sequencing, or (b) transient negative visible capacity for one tenant while the async backfill resolves. This is especially visible for reserved-units anchored to monthly epochs and when cross-region clock skew occurs.

Proposal (Commit-Split with Escrowed Micro-Commit):
Introduce a small-state protocol for reserved-capacity handoffs that guarantees visible invariants while keeping latency low:
1) Escrow phase: Source pool atomically places an "escrow" hold for the transfer amount in a shadow ledger keyed by transfer-id and epoch. The tenant's visible available decreases by the escrow amount but is marked as "pending-out".
2) Progressive handoff: Destination pool accepts the escrow via a two-phase handshake. On accept, destination creates a mirror shadow entry marked "pending-in." Visible metrics for the destination do not count pending-in until final commit unless the handshake completes within a configured hedge window.
3) Commit split / fallback: If two overlapping transfers target intersecting slices, the protocol performs a deterministic split ordering by transfer-id and epoch timestamp. If the handshake cannot complete within hedge-window (due to region outage or lag), the escrow automatically falls back to a conservative soft-credit path: allow destination to consume up to a configurable percentage of pending-in (hedge ratio) while tagging usage for post-facto reconciliation and potential credit adjustment.
4) Reconciliation & audit trail: A background reconciler consumes shadow ledgers and produces an immutable transfer record, applying final debits/credits and emitting correction events for any hedged consumption. All steps produce idempotent tombstones to ensure safe retries.

Design goals and invariants:
- Never present final visible overcommit beyond a small hedged window (configurable, default 5s) without an explicit tag and audit trail.
- Avoid negative available balance for a tenant that completed a transfer without a failed commit; in failure cases show explicit "pending-out" + reason rather than negative numbers.
- Support cross-region transfers with clock skew tolerance and deterministic tie-breakers.
- Telemetry: emit per-transfer lifecycle events (escrow_created, handshake_accepted, commit_applied, fallback_hedged, reconcile_completed) with transfer-id and affected ledger keys.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit & integration tests that simulate concurrent overlapping transfers and assert ledger invariants hold (no more than hedge_ratio overcommit).
- E2E canary showing zero billing discrepancies for a 48-hour window on synthetic high-rps tenant traffic vs baseline reconciliation job.
- Telemetry dashboards for transfer lifecycle with alert on reconcile latency > 2 minutes.
- Rollout under feature flag with deterministic kill switch that reverts to existing eventual protocol and triggers backfill reconciliation job.

Implementation notes:
- Introduce lightweight shadow-ledger table partitioned by epoch + transfer-id (TTL 90d). Keep operations idempotent using (transfer-id, attempt) tuples.
- Hedge ratio default 0.05 (5%) configurable per-tenant / per-plan. For enterprise reserved customers default is 0.0 unless explicitly enabled.
- Use existing lease manager to fence competing commits; if leader election fails fall back to ledger-level optimistic CAS with tombstone replay.
- Backfill job will run at low priority to convert hedged consumption into final debits and issue corrective credit notes when applicable.

Rollback plan:
- Feature flagged rollout; disable flag immediately to return to legacy path. Run backfill reconciler to translate any in-flight escrows into final ledger state. Monitor billing delta and customer tickets for 72 hours post-disable.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Hedge visibility: how prominently should guarded hedged consumption appear on tenant console (we propose explicit "pending hedged usage" line item).
- Complexity vs benefit: this adds another code path (shadow ledger) and reconciliation surface; weigh against frequency of overlapping transfers in production.

Estimated effort and milestones:
- Design + eng. spec: 2 days (done)
- Core protocol implementation + unit tests: 5d
- Integration & cross-region tests: 3d
- Canary/observability + rollout: 2d
- Total: ~12 engineer-days spread across 2 sprints
comments: 2026-03-02 - Marco Liu: Initial implementation branch created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123. WIP: escrow table schema and basic handshake messages. Leaving TODOs for tie-breaker policy.

2026-03-03 - Priya Natarajan (PM): We should flag enterprise reserved customers to opt-out of hedging by default. Also add a visible console label for hedged usage per tenant. Opened design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RD/Commit-Split+Escrow+Design

2026-03-05 - Security review (Jake Morris): Reviewed shadow ledger storage. No secret material stored; recommend audit log retention settings and KMS policy for reconciler credentials. Marking security_review_required=false but add ACL checks.

2026-03-07 - QA (Elena Torres): End-to-end tests created for overlapping transfers and heavy racy loads. Found race that caused duplicate handshake acceptance if leader re-elected; added idempotency token to handshake accept flow.

2026-03-09 - Marco Liu: Canary started in us-west-2 on 2 reserved pools (staging). Observed one fallback_hedged event due to transient zone-restart; reconciler completed and produced a corrective credit message. No customer-visible billing delta observed in 24h.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Reviewed and signed off on PR readiness. Next step: expand canary to eu-central-1 and run 48h synthetic traffic. Schedule postmortem template if discrepancies observed.
